title: Buying equipment from the shop computer
target: How to buy paint, tools, vehicles and fittings in Supermarket Simulator: why the computer has a viewer for each kind of thing rather than one list, where the vending machines are filed, and what the computer's screens are built on.
version: 1.6.0 (223), read from the copy of the game this site was built from (see the sources page)
prerequisites: A shop that is open with a computer placed
Enough money for what you intend to buy
Somewhere to put the thing once it arrives

steps.do: Start at the computer rather than looking for a catalogue in a menu.
steps.because: the computer is an object in the shop with a desk of its own, so buying equipment happens where the machine stands (T_SuperMarketComputer_AlbedoTransparency, T_SuperMarketComputerDesk_AlbedoTransparency)

steps.do: Expect a different viewer for each kind of thing instead of one long list.
steps.because: the shop floor has a viewer of its own and the furniture has another, so looking over what you own and buying something new are separate screens (FloorViewer, FurnituresViewer)

steps.do: Look for tools in their own viewer and their own kind of sale entry.
steps.because: tools are filed as a catalogue of their own rather than as ordinary stock (ToolsViewer, ToolSalesItem)

steps.do: Do not go to the stock list for a vehicle.
steps.because: vehicles have a viewer of their own, so what you drive is bought where the game keeps it rather than beside the groceries (VehiclesViewer)

steps.do: Treat paint as a purchase rather than a service.
steps.because: paint is sold as an item of its own, so it arrives as something you then use rather than as a job done for you (PaintSalesItem)

steps.do: Buy floors from their own entry and check them in their own viewer.
steps.because: flooring is filed as its own kind of sale entry rather than as a general fitting (FloorSalesItem, FloorViewer)

steps.do: Do not forget where the vending machines are kept.
steps.because: vending machines have a tab of their own on the computer, apart from the rest of the fittings (VendingMachineTab, VendingMachineComputerSlot)

steps.do: Expect the computer's screens to behave like windows rather than like full-screen menus.
steps.because: its screens are windows drawn on a desktop canvas of their own, so they open over one another rather than replacing the whole view (AppWindow, DesktopCanvas)

steps.do: Expect pricing to have its own controls inside the machine.
steps.because: the computer carries a handler for pricing controls rather than relying on a general input path (PricingControllerHandler)

steps.do: Plan where the thing will go before you buy it.
steps.because: what you buy is an object you then place, and placement is its own step rather than part of buying (VendingMachinePlacementDeadZone, VendingMachineTransformCalculator)

commonMistakes: Searching the stock list for a vehicle or a tool.
Expecting one catalogue to hold every kind of purchase.
Buying paint and expecting the game to apply it for you.
Treating the computer's screens as full-screen menus that replace each other.
sources: A local copy of the game, read only. Grounding for each step is on the technical reference pages; no number is estimated.
